summary_rationale: Manorama Industries has successfully transitioned from a low-margin forest-seed trader into a vertically integrated specialty-fats and Cocoa Butter Equivalent (CBE) manufacturer with 47,500 MTPA fractionation capacity at Birkoni (~85% utilized in Q2 FY27), proprietary Indian tribal and West African shea sourcing, and 3-to-5-year OEM approvals from global confectionery and cosmetic leaders. Revenue scaled nearly 9.4x from FY17 to ₹1,367 Cr in FY26 (₹1,617 Cr TTM; Q2 FY27 ₹458.86 Cr, +41.9% YoY, ~85% volume-led) with 25.8%–26.4% operating margins, 34.9% ROCE, and a decisive cash-flow inflection in FY26 (CFO +₹250 Cr, 92% CFO/EBITDA, FCF +₹196 Cr) reinforced by a ₹500 Cr QIP (zero deviations per CRISIL). KPI health remains PASS_WITH_WATCH due to structurally high seasonal inventory days (369 days in FY26), recurring H1 working-capital debt spikes (₹518 Cr in Sep 2026), single-site Birkoni plant concentration, West African raw shea export bans/levies (CFA 200/kg in Burkina Faso) driving up to ₹350 Cr in Sahel subsidiary funding, the pending ₹20.64 Cr Customs Section 108 inquiry (UAE PMF CEPA), promoter-owned Manorama Africa Limited RPT governance (₹200 Cr FY27 limit), and the November 12, 2026 executive transition to MD Deep Saraf and Chairman Mudit Kumar Singh.
